title: ServiceNow Zero-Copy Querying of Enterprise Data in Microsoft OneLake (Preview)
summary: Fabric Updates Blog post announcing a ServiceNow Workflow Data Fabric connector that reads OneLake data directly through Iceberg-compatible table APIs. The angle for Atlas readers is what the integration says about OneLake's open-standards query surface, not the ServiceNow product pitch itself.
audience: Architects and platform owners evaluating how non-Fabric SaaS or third-party query engines can consume OneLake data without ETL, and anyone tracking OneLake's Iceberg REST Catalog compatibility.
why_it_matters: Demonstrates a concrete, named third-party consumer of OneLake's Iceberg Table APIs, reinforcing that OneLake's zero-copy story extends beyond Fabric-native engines to external SaaS platforms and open-source query engines.
takeaways: OneLake now has at least one named operational-SaaS consumer (ServiceNow) reading data in place via open table APIs, not a proprietary connector.
The integration is explicitly built on the Apache Iceberg REST Catalog standard rather than a Fabric-specific protocol.
This is a preview-stage feature as of the post's publication, not yet generally available.
The same open API surface is described as usable by other engines (Trino, DuckDB, Spark), positioning OneLake as a multi-engine data foundation rather than a Fabric-only store.

claims.text: ServiceNow Workflow Data Fabric ships a zero-copy connector that lets ServiceNow read data stored in OneLake in place, without moving or duplicating it into ServiceNow.
This ServiceNow OneLake connector is called out as a preview capability at time of publication, not a generally available feature.

The connector is built on OneLake Table APIs that implement the Apache Iceberg REST Catalog standard, letting external engines discover and query OneLake tables through an open, non-proprietary interface.

Because the Iceberg REST Catalog interface is open, engines beyond ServiceNow's connector - named examples include Trino, DuckDB, and Apache Spark - can query OneLake data using the same Table APIs without custom, engine-specific integration code.

The integration pattern positions OneLake as a shared governed data foundation for operational workflow tools (like ServiceNow) as well as analytics and AI workloads, so the same underlying dataset can back incident enrichment, field-service context, supply-chain visibility, or AI workflow assistants without separate copies per use case.

Microsoft frames this ServiceNow integration as one example of a broader direction: enabling any partner or application to build on OneLake through open standards (Iceberg REST Catalog) rather than requiring proprietary Fabric-specific integration layers.
